chapter: Leaving Coltrane: Blakey, Ellington and big bands
title: Cosmos and playing with Hubert Laws and Andrew White
summary: Tyner praises Hubert Laws's range and Brown notes Andrew White, in discussing the expanded ensemble on Cosmos.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: And then I’m holding in my hand now, McCoy Tyner, and this is a Blue Note re-issue, Cosmos. And this also has expanded ensembles insofar as beyond the trio and quartet format, I’m looking at “Asian Lullaby” and “Hope.”. Yourself, Herbie Lewis, Freddie Waits, Gary Bartz, which was a long-term association, Hubert Laws--

Yeah, I like Hubert because he played in the symphony orchestra. He could sit down and play anything, he could play jazz, he could play classics, he was just so flexible and his tone was phenomenal and he was a gentleman, impeccable person, I really liked that.
Seems you were in good company.

You were in that number, and then Andrew White was on this on oboe and Andrew is a story in himself because I know he played with Elvin’s group and Ken and I saw him in Germany. Andrew is a real character.
Well, that’s what some of us are (laughs) and some of us hope that we’re not (laughs).
